about.title: About this nutrition calculator
intro: This is a free online nutrition calculator: pick from common foods and Foods for Special Medical Purposes (FSMP), enter the amounts, and the tool automatically sums the energy, protein, fat and carbohydrate of a meal or a day, comparing them against Dietary Reference Intakes (DRI).

It suits ordinary people who want to know how much they've eaten and whether their nutrition is balanced, as well as nutrition students and frontline workers who need quick estimates. No sign-up; data stays in your own browser.
basis: Regular foods use common per-100g reference values for estimation, not a specific product's label.
Reference intakes come from public standards such as the Chinese Dietary Reference Intakes (DRIs).
FSMP data is compiled from manufacturer labels, instructions and public registration records, with a source noted for each entry.
use: Search and select the food or medical food you ate.
View the auto-summed energy and macronutrients below, and the comparison with DRI.
Use the result as a reference for adjusting your everyday diet.

faq.a: Results are estimates based on common reference values, useful for a rough picture. The same food varies by variety, origin and cooking, so treat the numbers as a reference.

faq.q: Can it be a basis for medical or prescription decisions?
faq.a: No. This tool is for nutrition education and self-understanding, not medical advice. For illness or special needs, follow your doctor or a registered dietitian.

faq.q: Where does the medical-food data come from?
faq.a: From manufacturers' public labels, instructions and registration records; verify the latest product information before clinical use.

about.note: This tool is for nutritional education and reference only and does not constitute medical advice.

daily.title: Daily Needs
daily.subtitle: Estimates BMR / TDEE via the Mifflin-St Jeor formula and compares against Chinese DRI 2023 recommendations

about.title: About the daily nutrient needs estimate
intro: This tool estimates your basal metabolic rate (BMR) and total daily energy expenditure (TDEE) from your sex, age, weight, height and activity level, then combines them with a goal of losing, maintaining or gaining weight to give a daily energy target, a macronutrient split, and reference values for key micronutrients.
It turns the question of how much energy and nutrition you need in a day into concrete numbers, useful when planning your everyday diet.
basis: BMR uses the Mifflin-St Jeor equation, one of the more commonly used and robust estimating equations.
TDEE multiplies BMR by an activity factor (from sedentary to high intensity).
Macros are split around the midpoint of the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range (AMDR); micronutrients reference DRI recommended intakes.
use: Choose your sex and enter age, weight and height.
Choose a goal: maintain, lose or gain weight.
View BMR, TDEE, the daily energy target, and reference values for protein, fat, carbs and micronutrients.

faq.q: What's the difference between BMR and TDEE?
faq.a: BMR is the energy your body needs at complete rest to sustain basic functions; TDEE adds daily activity and exercise on top, and is closer to what you actually need each day.
Equation estimates are a good starting point for most healthy adults, but individual differences, illness and special life stages affect real needs — adjust based on weight changes and how you feel.

faq.q: Can I use it directly to lose weight?
faq.a: As a reference, yes; weight loss needs a gentle, sustained reduction in total energy while keeping nutrition balanced. Those with underlying disease or on medication should follow medical advice.

about.note: Estimates are for reference only and cannot replace individualized assessment by a doctor or registered dietitian.

about.title: About the FSMP library
intro: Foods for Special Medical Purposes (FSMP) are formula foods designed for the nutritional needs of specific diseases or medical conditions. This library lets you browse different categories of FSMP by disease, understanding roughly which situations they suit, their formula features and nutritional basis.
The information is compiled from public labels and manufacturer instructions and presented by category (not as brand recommendations), to help professionals and caregivers get oriented quickly.
basis: Each entry notes its source, registration number, regulatory category and market.
Indications map to disease categories (diabetes, renal, oncology, hepatic, peri-operative, pediatric, etc.).
Information comes from manufacturer labels, instructions and public registration records — for orientation only, not a substitute for the latest product information.
use: Choose the disease or medical-condition category you're interested in.
Browse the formula categories and features under it.
View the nutritional basis, source and other information.
When needed, add an item to the calculator to estimate nutrient intake.

faq.a: It's a formula food designed for the nutritional needs of a specific disease or medical condition, usually to be used under the guidance of a doctor or clinical dietitian.

faq.q: Can I buy and use these based on the library alone?
faq.a: Not advised. Whether to use one, which category, and how much should be decided by a doctor or registered/clinical dietitian based on the specific condition.
It's compiled from public labels and manufacturer instructions with sources noted; but products change, so verify the latest information before clinical use.

about.note: This library presents information by category; it is not a product recommendation or medical advice. Verify and follow medical advice before clinical use.

about.title: About the clinical nutrition assessment
intro: This page runs a structured nutritional assessment using deterministic clinical rules: body mass index (BMI), malnutrition judgment based on GLIM 2018, NRS-2002 nutritional risk screening, plus energy and protein target estimates and interpretation of common lab values — with an optional AI deep-dive report.
It is aimed at clinical-nutrition learning and work. All rule-based calculations run locally in your browser; this is an educational and supportive tool, not a replacement for a doctor's diagnosis.
basis: GLIM 2018: at least 1 phenotypic criterion plus at least 1 etiologic criterion.
NRS-2002 (Kondrup 2003): a score of 3 or more indicates nutritional risk.
ESPEN: energy about 25-35 kcal/kg/d, protein about 1.0-2.0 g/kg/d (by stress level).
Disease-specific adjustments per guidelines (e.g., low protein for non-dialysis chronic kidney disease).
use: Enter assessment data such as height, weight, diagnosis and labs (use a pseudonym; don't enter real identifiable information).
View the rule-based assessment results and nutritional targets generated automatically.
If needed, generate the AI deep-dive as a supplementary reference.

faq.a: No. The results are rule-based outputs from public guidelines, for education and support; final diagnosis and treatment must be decided by the attending physician.

faq.q: Is the data I enter safe?
faq.a: Assessment data stays in your browser and is not stored on the server. When you generate the AI interpretation, the entered content is relayed via the server to a third-party LLM, so don't enter real patient-identifiable information.
It's an explanatory supplement to the rule-based results; it can only interpret, not modify, those numbers, and likewise is not a basis for diagnosis or treatment.

about.note: This page is for nutritional education and supportive reference only; it is not a diagnosis or prescription. Make decisions under the guidance of an attending physician or registered dietitian.

about.title: About NutriCalc
about.intro: NutriCalc is an independent, free, open-source evidence-based nutrition site focused on clinical nutrition and everyday balanced eating, with a bilingual interface and a dedicated module for Foods for Special Medical Purposes (FSMP).
about.mission: We aim to turn nutrition knowledge scattered across guidelines, textbooks and official sources into tools and plain-language articles that ordinary people and frontline workers can use. All calculation logic and articles are grounded in public, authoritative sources, with the goal of being understandable, verifiable and actionable — not a replacement for the individualized judgment of a physician or registered dietitian. This project sells no food or supplements, accepts no sponsored content, and has no commercial ties to the brands it lists.
principles: Evidence first: each recommendation maps to a guideline, official standard or public reference value where possible; no wellness fads or alternative-medicine content.
No brand recommendations: for medical foods we describe categories and use cases only, never specific products.
Flag uncertainty: where individualized judgment is needed, we explicitly say "to be confirmed by the attending physician or a registered dietitian".
Education, not diagnosis: content is for health education and does not constitute diagnosis or a prescription.
Privacy: assessment data is processed only in your browser; pages with patient data load no ads or third-party tracking.
Transparency: the project is open source, so its logic and data can be inspected and checked.
about.sources_intro: Our calculation logic and articles draw mainly on the following authoritative sources:
sources: ESPEN guidelines on enteral and parenteral nutrition
Dietary Guidelines for Chinese Residents (2022), Chinese Nutrition Society
China NHC Dietary Guidelines (2023) for specific conditions (diabetes, dyslipidemia, etc.)
about.tools_intro: The site is built around being accurate, understandable and practical:
tools: Nutrition calculator: pick common foods and medical foods to auto-sum energy, protein, fat and carbs against DRI reference values.
Clinical assessment: deterministic rules based on BMI, GLIM and NRS-2002 give nutritional risk and energy/protein targets, plus an optional AI deep-dive.
Daily needs: estimate BMR/TDEE and DRI targets from height, weight, age and activity level.
FSMP library: browse category-level information on medical foods by condition, compiled from public labels and manufacturer instructions.
Nutrition tips: evidence-based articles covering disease-specific diets, special populations, nutrients and food safety.
about.data_intro: Our data falls into two distinct types, each labeled accordingly:
data: Regular foods: common per-100g reference values for estimation, not specific product labels.

Medical foods (FSMP): compiled from manufacturer labels, instructions and public registration records; each entry notes its source, registration number and regulatory category — verify before clinical use.
DRI values: from public standards such as the Chinese Dietary Reference Intakes.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: NutriCalc ("we") respects your privacy. This policy explains how we handle information when you use this site.

sections.h: 1. We do not collect account information
sections.p: This site requires no registration or login, and does not collect your email, phone number, name, or other account information.
To make the tool usable, your browser stores the following information — this data stays on your device and is never uploaded to our servers:
ul: Items selected in the calculator (foods / medical foods)
Admin token (only when you actively enable admin mode)
sections.after: You can remove all of this at any time via your browser's "Clear site data".

sections.p: When you actively click "Generate AI deep report", the data you have entered in the assessment form is relayed via our server to one of the following LLM APIs:
sections.after: Our server does not store this data — it is forwarded and discarded. Third-party LLM providers have their own privacy policies. Do not enter real patient-identifying information (name, ID number, medical record number, etc.); use aliases or pseudonyms.

sections.p: We use Cloudflare Turnstile to verify you are not a bot; Turnstile may collect browser signals — see Cloudflare's privacy policy. Our server keeps a per-IP counter of AI requests per day for rate-limiting; the counter is automatically cleared after 24 hours.
This site uses Cloudflare Web Analytics — a cookieless analytics service that does not identify individuals. It aggregates visits, pages, referrers, and browser types only.

This site sets no tracking cookies of its own. When content pages (articles, about, home) display Google AdSense ads, Google and its partners may use cookies or similar technologies to serve and measure ads; you can manage personalized ads in Google Ads Settings, and users in the EEA / UK / Switzerland are shown Google's consent message first. The assessment, daily-needs, and FSMP-library pages load no ads or third-party tracking scripts. All other tool data is stored only in your browser's localStorage as described in section 2.

Since we do not store identifiable data about you, no "deletion request" is required. You can clear your browser localStorage at any time to remove local data. For questions, email contact@125261.xyz.
This policy may be updated occasionally; the "Last updated" date at the top of this page reflects the latest change.

disclaimer.title: Medical Disclaimer
disclaimer.intro: NutriCalc is not a medical device and does not replace professional medical advice. Please understand the following before relying on any calculation or AI output.

sections.p: This tool is intended for nutrition education and calculation demonstration. It is not a medical device under any applicable regulation and does not substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

Clinical calculations on this site (GLIM malnutrition diagnosis, NRS-2002 risk screening, energy and protein targets, etc.) implement published clinical guidelines, but the outputs are reference values only and do not represent clinical judgment for any specific patient.
The "AI Deep Interpretation" is produced by a third-party large language model. It can hallucinate, be outdated, or be wrong. It does not constitute a prescription, medical order, or medical advice.

The FSMP library includes product data transcribed from public labels or manufacturer instructions, but formulas, registration status, and package sizes may change. Food nutrient values are common reference figures and may differ from actual product labels.

sections.h: 5. Do not enter identifiable patient data
sections.p: Do not enter real patient names, ID numbers, medical record numbers, or any other identifying information into the assessment form. Use aliases or pseudonyms. See the Privacy Policy for details.
If you are experiencing any of the following, seek medical care immediately rather than rely on this tool:
ul: Severe malnutrition or significant weight loss
Acute symptoms (uncontrolled vomiting, altered consciousness, breathing difficulty, etc.)
Adjustment of a treatment plan for a chronic disease

sections.p: We are not liable for any consequences arising from your use of this site or the information it contains. Clinical decisions must be made by qualified medical professionals based on the full clinical picture.
